original_question: Problem 6.8 (S. Vũ Ngo.c). Find natural examples of integrable systems in classical mechanics with non-trivial Duistermaat–Chern classes.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 6.8 (S. Vũ Ngọc), in "Poisson geometry and action-angle variables" (v2/journal pagination: page 34).
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official open problem almost verbatim: it has the correct problem number, attribution to S. Vũ Ngọc, the restriction to classical mechanics, and the exact target of finding natural examples with non-trivial Duistermaat-Chern class.
missing_details: The nearby context says this is specifically a symplectic/global action-angle problem, even though Poisson methods may be needed.
It is implicit that the Duistermaat-Chern class here is Duistermaat’s Chern obstruction to globalizing action-angle coordinates for the regular Liouville torus fibration.
For a stand-alone formulation, it helps to say explicitly that "non-trivial" means nonzero.

The surrounding paragraph adds an important scope restriction: the Chern class always vanishes for systems with two degrees of freedom, so the first genuinely open range starts at three degrees of freedom.
The paper also explains why "natural" is part of the question: arbitrary Chern classes can be constructed by hand, but the authors want examples arising naturally from classical mechanics.

To make the question self-contained, one should indicate that the relevant class belongs to the regular Liouville torus fibration of a Liouville-integrable Hamiltonian system with compact regular tori.
refined_question: Find a natural finite-dimensional Liouville-integrable Hamiltonian system from classical mechanics, in the symplectic setting and with compact regular Liouville tori, whose regular torus fibration has nonzero Duistermaat-Chern class, i.e. a genuine Chern obstruction to the existence of global action-angle coordinates. Since this class vanishes for two degrees of freedom, the first interesting cases begin in three degrees of freedom.
justification: The draft is already the exact official target, so the refinement stays extremely close to the paper and only makes implicit context explicit. The preceding paragraph to Problem 6.8 identifies the Duistermaat-Chern class as one of the two obstructions to global action-angle coordinates, states that the problem is in the symplectic case, notes that the class vanishes in two degrees of freedom, and emphasizes that the missing ingredient is a natural classical-mechanics example rather than an ad hoc construction. No ambient ring, field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, operator, or "for sufficiently large" quantifier data occur in this problem; the missing information is geometric context, not algebraic specification. The paper gives no classical equivalent reformulation; Problem 7.4 is only a quantum analogue.
